video_caption: The video features a split screen, showcasing an app called "Clouds of Bubbles" on both an Android Wear smartwatch (left) and a Samsung smartphone (right). Initially, a hand interacts with the smartwatch, tapping colorful circular icons that function as app launchers, settings (including brightness and watch face options), and a contact list, which then opens Google Maps. Concurrently on the right, a hand swipes through various colorful circular app icons on the smartphone, which also transitions to a contacts view with circular profile pictures and a web article from "BUSINESS INSIDER" titled "This app can make your cheaper Google smartwatch look just like an Apple Watch." The smartwatch then displays hexagonal icons and a watch face with different sized bubbles showing utility information like battery life and date. The smartphone similarly cycles through various app layouts and a "Voice changer with effects" app. The video concludes with a title card, showing the smartwatch with a busy bubble watch face and the smartphone with more app bubbles, accompanied by the text "Android Wear: 4:10" and the "Clouds of Bubbles" logo, indicating a specific segment of the video and the app being advertised.

A right hand holding a black stylus interacts with a black Samsung smartphone lying on a wooden surface. The phone's screen displays a grid of colorful circular app icons. An overlay on the bottom left reads "Android Wear: 4:10" with a play arrow, and a circular smartwatch face is visible in the top left corner. A logo in the top right corner shows a grid of colorful circles with the text "Clouds of Bubbles On your phone and watch". The hand taps the phone screen, causing a menu to appear at the bottom with options "Wallpapers," "Widgets," and "Settings." The overlay text changes to "1 Add widget." The hand then taps "Widgets," and the screen transitions to a list of available widgets. The hand with the stylus proceeds to drag a widget labeled "App Bubble Cloud" from this list.

A person uses a stylus to interact with a Samsung smartphone lying on a wooden table, with a pencil icon to the left of the phone. The phone displays an "App bubble" customization menu for an app called "WatchOut." The person taps to change the border color, selecting green from a color palette. Next, they tap "Touch bubble to change image" and select an icon from an "Icon pack Moonshine" menu, searching for "bird" and choosing a red bird icon. The bubble preview updates with the new green border and bird icon. The person then adjusts the "Adjust bubble size" slider before tapping a red-outlined trash can icon to delete the bubble. The pencil icon on the left transitions to a trash can icon as another "App bubble" menu appears for an app called "Attopedia," which the person also deletes by tapping the trash can icon. Finally, a red arrow appears on the phone screen, pointing to the previously customized green-bordered bubble with the red bird icon. Throughout the video, a logo "Clouds of Bubbles On your phone and watch" is visible in the top right corner.

The video opens with a Samsung smartphone lying on a wooden table, displaying an application interface with numerous circular icons arranged in a "cloud" formation, centered on the screen, with a red arrow pointing to one of the central bubbles. The top right corner features a logo that reads "Clouds of Bubbles" (Clouds of Bubbles) with text below saying "On your phone and watch" (On your phone and watch). A hand, holding a stylus, then interacts with the phone screen, first touching the upper part of the screen to adjust settings, causing the circular icons to rearrange. Two blue curved arrow icons (🔄) appear as an overlay on the left to indicate this action. The stylus then taps a circular plus icon in the upper right, and a larger yellow-bordered circular plus icon (⨁) appears on the left as an overlay while the phone screen transitions to a "Configure App Bubble Cloud" settings menu. Within this menu, the stylus scrolls through options, and an overlay appears showing a "before" and "after" comparison of the app's background changing from opaque to transparent, with a yellow down arrow (⬇️) indicating the change, followed by the stylus selecting a color from a color picker pop-up. Next, the hand checks the "Auto populate" checkbox in the "Cloud properties" section; simultaneously, an animated graphic overlay on the left illustrates the "Auto populate" feature, showing new app icons (represented by various app logos) automatically appearing in the bubble cloud after being installed from the Play Store. The stylus then navigates to an "Add Tasker bubble" section, and a gray gear icon with a yellow lightning bolt (⚡) appears as an overlay on the left. A pop-up menu listing various Tasker tasks such as "BAS: BT off", "BAS: Day", and "BAS: Drive" (BAS: BT off, BAS: Day, BAS: Drive) appears, from which the stylus selects one and taps "Add". Finally, an overlay appears on the left, labeled "Colorful Bubbles Icon Pack:", demonstrating a visual change in the app icons from a standard look to a more stylized, colorful design, with a yellow arrow pointing to the right (➡️). The stylus interacts with an "Icon pack" dropdown menu on the phone, selecting "Colorful Bubbles Icon Pack" (Colorful Bubbles Icon Pack) from a list of options. A confirmation dialog appears with the text: "Refresh bubble images. Click 'Refresh images' to fetch new icons for all bubbles in the cloud. Since you recently modified the background color, bubble colors will be updated for better contrast (cancel and refresh later to keep current bubble colors)." The stylus then taps "Refresh images," and the video concludes with the app's bubble cloud now displaying the updated colorful icon pack.

A person's right hand, holding a black stylus, interacts with a Samsung smartphone placed on a light brown wooden table. The phone screen displays the "Bubble Cloud Settings" menu. The person scrolls down and taps a checkbox next to "Hide pencil (2-tap background)." A dialog box appears, stating: "When the pencil is hidden, you will have to double tap on an empty area of the widget to invoke delete/configure mode. Hide pencil? OK Cancel." (The pencil icon is for editing widgets.) The person taps "OK," and the phone's home screen, displaying multiple circular "bubble" widgets over a blue gradient background, appears. A graphic of a red-crossed-out pencil, along with the text "Hide pencil:", is shown on the left. The person demonstrates that the editing pencil is now hidden but can still be accessed by double-tapping an empty area of the widget, which brings up red configuration borders. The screen then changes to highlight different types of bubble clouds: "Apps" (with an Android robot icon), "Contacts" (with a person icon), and "Bookmarks" (with a bookmark ribbon icon), showing corresponding bubble clouds on the phone. The person then demonstrates adding a bookmark by navigating to a Yahoo webpage in the Chrome browser, tapping the three-dot menu, selecting "Share...", and choosing "Add Bookmark Bubble." The webpage content visually transforms into a bubble and is added to a widget. Lastly, the video demonstrates the "Save as orphan" feature by long-pressing an existing bubble widget and choosing "Save as orphan" from a pop-up menu. A full-screen dialog titled "Merge orphaned bubbles into:" appears, listing saved bubble sets. The person taps "Save as orphan" at the bottom right. After the widget is removed, the text "Restore" appears with an Android robot icon. The person drags a new app bubble widget onto the home screen, and a dialog box titled "Restore bubbles from deleted widget..." appears, prompting to "Add bubbles" to restore the previously saved bubbles.

The video opens with a close-up of a black smartwatch on a green fabric surface, displaying an app drawer with octagonal icons, including a calendar icon showing "WED 20". Overlay text on the right reads "Launcher for Android Wear" and "1. App drawer 2. Watch face". At 0:12, the watch screen changes to a settings interface for the drawer, with options like "left," "off," and "right" for "Swipe-in or 2x tap edge," and a slider to adjust the handle size. A finger interacts with these settings, dragging the slider and selecting "right" for the drawer's position. A horizontal red dashed line appears across the screen at 0:19, highlighting the upper half of the watch's edge as sensitive. At 0:22, the watch face (a black analog clock with "moto" branding) is shown, and a finger attempts to swipe from the bottom edge, resulting in a red circle with a cross (🚫) indicating failure. Subsequently, at 0:25, the finger successfully swipes from the upper right edge, bringing up the app drawer, and a green checkmark (✅) appears. This is repeated at 0:28 (failure) and 0:29 (success). The video concludes at 0:31 with a different, gold-cased smartwatch with a colorful band displayed within a watch box, showing a different watch face with various data bubbles (e.g., battery percentage, steps, temperature), while the app drawer and watch face text overlays remain.

The video showcases a smart watch, gold/rose gold with blue and orange straps, resting in a beige, velvet-lined watch box. The watch face displays a circular arrangement of colorful "bubbles" acting as icons, with a central sun/gear motif. Text overlays identify "1. App drawer" and "2. Watch face" at the bottom left, and a logo "Clouds of Bubbles On your phone and watch" at the top right. A finger interacts with the watch face, tapping bubbles; tapping the lock icon twice brings up text prompts: "Long tap to toggle auto-lock" and "Change lock behaviour in Cloud Editor (in phone app)." Tapping a green "88%" bubble (battery indicator) shows a brief animation, and tapping another bubble (bottom left) launches a "Settings" screen ("Adjust brightness," "Change watch face"). The screen then transitions back to the bubble watch face, and an overlay "Launcher: (showing a clock icon)" appears. Tapping the central bubble now activates an app drawer, allowing swipes to reveal more app icons. The watch face reverts to the bubble display, and the overlay changes to "Normal: (showing a black clock icon)." In this mode, swiping down brings up "Notifications," swiping left shows "Cards," and swiping up or right returns to the main watch face, demonstrating standard watch functionalities. Tapping the battery bubble again launches a "Flashlight" app, and swipes briefly reveal the app drawer before returning to the bubble watch face.

The video segment features a smartwatch, likely a Huawei Watch GT series with a gold-colored bezel and a blue strap, resting in a cream-colored watch box with a plush interior, situated on a light brown wooden surface. Overlaid text at the bottom left reads "1. App drawer" and "2. Watch face," suggesting the video will demonstrate functionalities related to these aspects. In the top right corner, a logo shows colorful bubbles with the text "Clouds of Bubbles" and "On your phone and watch." The watch face dynamically transitions between an active mode, displaying digital time (e.g., 08:44, then 08:35, then 08:12), date (FRI 12), battery percentage (e.g., 91%, 95%, 96%, 88%), steps (800), and various other metrics within solid, colorful circular icons. It then switches to an "ambient mode" where the watch face either shows hollow versions of these circular icons or hides some of them completely, with the digital time also changing to reflect this state, and later transitioning to an analog clock display with hollow icons, all described as a "burning prevention measure."

The video segment features a Moto 360 smartwatch on the left and a smartphone on the right displaying an app interface. An arrow points from the "App-drawer" option selected on the phone to the smartwatch, indicating a setting. A hand with a finger then interacts with the smartwatch, which displays app icons arranged in a circular "bubble cloud" style. A graphic on the right introduces "Clouds of Bubbles / On your phone and watch" and shows a yellow star icon, representing a "favorites" cloud of apps. As the finger swipes, a different set of app icons appears, now horizontally scrollable, represented by a brown 9-dot icon, which is the "archive" cloud. The video then demonstrates long-pressing an app icon on the watch to move it between the archive and favorites clouds, with an animated double-headed arrow between the brown 9-dot and yellow star icons on the right symbolizing this transfer. Next, the video shows a hand interacting with the watch on a green fabric, demonstrating brightness control. An "A" icon on the watch, paired with the text "Auto brightness" (meaning: automatic brightness adjustment) on the right, is tapped, and a vertical slider appears, showing the brightness change. A different, gold smartwatch with a blue strap is then shown, also featuring an "A" icon, which here represents "Ambient brightness" (meaning: the brightness of the always-on display). Tapping it reveals a message "Set AMBIENT brightness" and then "Set ACTIVE brightness" as the slider is adjusted. Finally, the screen splits into two halves: a bright, sunny daytime scene on the left and a dark, starry nighttime scene on the right, both with a smartwatch and a vertical brightness slider. A stylized "D" icon with a sun/moon symbol appears next to each slider, illustrating how the watch face brightness can be adjusted and stored differently for day (bright) and night (dim, for example, in a theatre) to conserve battery or reduce distraction. The slider for the nighttime scene is set significantly lower.

The video segment opens on a warm, dark brown wooden surface, presenting a black smartwatch with a leather band lying flat on the left, next to a black Samsung smartphone on the right. The smartphone's screen displays an application interface titled "Bubble Cloud Settings" (not fully visible at the top, but implied by context), featuring sections like "Smart auto-layouts" and "Archive," each containing various grid-like arrangements of small, blue circular icons and a "Bubble spacing" slider below them. The smartwatch initially shows a watch face with four distinct square icons in its default layout. A hand, holding a silver stylus, then appears and interacts with the smartwatch screen. The watch face transforms, displaying a dense "random cloud of bubbles" — a multitude of small, colorful, circular app icons, with an analog clock face showing "FRI 14" at its center. The stylus taps on this dynamic cloud, causing the icons to shift and rearrange. Subsequently, the smartwatch screen quickly transitions to a more structured layout, presenting larger, predominantly square and some circular icons in a clear grid, while the central clock remains. The stylus continues to interact with these icons, demonstrating a fluid and responsive interface. The smartphone screen remains static throughout this interaction, showcasing the layout customization options available in the companion app.

The video displays a close-up of a silver smartwatch with a round screen on a person's wrist, alongside a mobile phone screen showing a "Wear Cloud Editor" application. The smartwatch's screen initially shows a pink circular icon with "800" (likely steps) inside, then transitions to a blue screen displaying "008" and subsequently a "Wear Stand up Alert" interface with "Inactivity tracking" and "Active hours" details. On the right, the phone screen lists various "bubbles" or app shortcuts: "Clock Bubble," "Wear Stand up Alert," "Task Manager," "Calendar," "Weather," "Find my Phone Battery Bubble," and more, each with an icon, name, and a numerical value (e.g., "+8"). A red arrow points to the "Calendar" entry, then to the information icon next to "Wear Stand up Alert." A pop-up titled "Assign Live-info" appears over the phone app list, showing multiple circular icons representing different data types (e.g., temperature, calendar, steps), and a red arrow highlights the "WED 19" (Wednesday 19th) calendar icon. The smartwatch then shows a colorful, complex watch face with a central analog clock and several small circular "bubbles" arranged around it, displaying information like "77%" (battery), "FRI 12" (Friday 12th - calendar), "800" (steps), and Wi-Fi/lock icons. Simultaneously, the phone app list updates, showing "Wear Stand up Alert" now labeled "STEPS" with a "800" icon, and a red arrow points to its information icon. The smartwatch screen changes to display a large "6°" and "3°" (temperatures) on a blue background, while the phone's "Weather" entry is highlighted, and a red arrow points to its information icon. Another "Assign Live-info" pop-up appears on the phone, with a red arrow pointing to a weather-related icon. The smartwatch then displays detailed weather information for "Budapest," showing "47°," "7mph," and "100%" on a blue background. The phone's "Weather" entry now shows "35° 19° TODAY" (temperatures) in its icon. As the app list on the phone scrolls down, a "Wifi Bubble (on - off - hotspot)" entry becomes visible, and a red arrow points to a small 'paper' icon next to it, indicating an action or detail for this bubble, while the smartwatch maintains its complex, informative watch face layout.

The video segment features a close-up of a person's wrist, wearing a black, round smartwatch with a vibrant, blue-themed interface that displays a clock, the date "FRI 12," and various circular app icons. A finger taps an icon resembling four squares, which transitions the watch face to a dark screen with glowing green app icons before opening a calculator app with a numeric keypad and basic operation symbols. Throughout this, a green circular graphic with white text appears in the top right corner of the screen, explaining the "STICKY OPEN" feature: "Double tap an app bubble to keep it on screen (automatically re-open when screen un-dims) Long tap time/lock on top to disable sticky mode". The watch repeatedly switches between the main app screen and the calculator app, demonstrating the sticky open function as the calculator reappears when the screen is active. At the 0:20 mark, the watch's interface changes to a more colorful design with yellow numbers "16 38" at the center, surrounded by various app icons, temperature readings (6°C), and battery percentage (84%). Simultaneously, a smaller inset video appears in the bottom right corner, showing a person in a white long-sleeved shirt checking the wrist of another person, who is wearing a rectangular black smartwatch. The "2x" playback speed indicator is visible in the top left throughout the segment, and the "Clouds of Bubbles" app logo is present in the top right.

The video segment showcases various features of the "Clouds of Bubbles" app on a smartwatch, initially displaying a person's wrist wearing a silver smartwatch with an analog clock face showing a red marker at 6 o'clock, with an inset image of a doctor checking a pulse, and the "Clouds of Bubbles" logo. The watch face then transitions to a vibrant, circular "bubble" launcher interface as a hand double-taps the screen, activating a voice search function indicated by a Google "G" logo and the text "Speak now" (0:08-0:14). Next, a smartwatch with a black strap is shown next to a black smartphone on a wooden surface; the watch's bubble launcher includes a phone battery icon (75% charged), and tapping it causes the phone to ring loudly and display the same bubble launcher interface (0:14-0:21). The scene shifts to a mobile phone screen displaying the "Wear Cloud Editor" app, where a user can add "Tasker bubbles" by selecting predefined tasks like "BUB: BCL play" and customizing their icons, such as a green play button, emphasizing the app's versatility (0:21-0:35). Subsequently, the silver smartwatch is shown charging on its side on a wooden table, and its display automatically rotates sideways to align with its orientation, accompanied by a charging icon (0:35-0:39). Finally, the smartwatch on the person's wrist displays a "Stand up" alert notification ("Fewer than 32 steps detected in the past 60 minutes"), and the watch vibrates; concurrently, a phone screen shows the "Bubble Cloud Settings" for a "Stand up Alert," allowing the user to configure inactivity tracking, notification cards, vibration settings, and active hours for the alert, with the person interacting with both the watch and phone to adjust these settings (0:39-0:49).

The video begins with a close-up shot of a black Samsung smartphone and a round, black smartwatch with a dark brown leather strap, resting on a wooden surface. A hand holding a silver stylus navigates the smartphone screen, which displays the "Bubble Cloud Settings" menu, tapping on "Wear contacts". The screen then changes to "Configure Contact Bubble Cloud," showing instructions on how to use the feature. Simultaneously, the smartwatch face, initially displaying a watch face, transforms to show multiple circular contact photos arranged in a "cloud" formation. A finger then taps one of the contact photos on the watch, revealing a larger central photo of a man named "Gergo Viczián" surrounded by smaller icons for calling, texting, and emailing. A text overlay appears, stating, "Default action set for contact. Long press to clear." The finger performs a long press on the contact photo, causing the contact options to disappear and the contact cloud to reappear. Next, the watch screen transitions to a voice input interface where "g how" is shown, which then completes to "how are you doing". This is followed by a screen displaying "Send?" with the message "how are you doing," and two yellow circular buttons—one with a cancel symbol and another with a checkmark for sending. The scene then transitions to a screenshot of the Google Play Store page for "Bubble Cloud Widgets and Mini Launcher for Android Wear" by DYNA Logix, rated PEGI 3, with an "Install" button. Text "Please" appears at the bottom of the screen, and then five yellow stars sequentially animate onto the screen from left to right, indicating a five-star rating, reinforcing the request for user reviews.
